newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products rally, gasoline demand perks up.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products rally, gasoline demand perks up.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly higher on Friday with demand perking up for gasoline after recent declines in lower octane grades.
Gasoline rose with some increased demand from northern Africa and eastern Mediterranean destinations for low octane, Eurograde and super unleaded grades, traders said.
Weaker prices may have encouraged some end-user demand as well as a stronger NWE market.
"The market itself is a bit weak but in the last couple of days there has been quite good demand for those three grades for cross-Med destinations," an Italian trader said.
The arb to NWE and the U.S. was shut, the trader added.
Gas oil including low sulphur diesel was inactive but traders reported extensive discussion over 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil.

They said five unsold heating oil cargoes, one Greek specification offered at cif high +$1, one Russian export grade offered at cif high +$3 as well as three unsold Romanian cargoes, were putting pressure on values with premiums barely steady at high cif +2 basis Genoa.
Some traders said all but one of six cargoes in the Turkish tender for 135,000 tonnes were covered.
Fuel oil prices were steady to slightly firmer, but traders said both high and low sulphur markets were on their way up.

Dealers saw a Syrian and a Spanish high sulphur cargo weighing on benchmark quotes, which undervalued the market by $5 per tonne. Arbitrage buyers were snapping up Italian Islands cargoes on floating prices, and one seller saw bids up to $111 fob for high density material.
Low sulphur markets were buoyed slightly by arbitrage buying, but the main bullish factor was Italy's purchase of around 250,000 tonnes this week. Traders expected Italy to continue buying heavily.
